problem: The line 'FR-01 The app shall show an alert within 30 s of an official outage message' is declared to pass because 'the clock start is named', but the start point (receipt of the message) is not actually stated. The exam traps later say the same phrasing is incomplete without 'from receipt of official message to visible alert', so the chapter contradicts itself.
fix: FR-01 The app shall show an alert within 30 s of receiving an official outage message. Say the clock starts when the message is received and stops when the alert is visible.

problem: The bullet list has eight sections, with Performance and Security written as one bullet. The figure stack has nine items and splits them into 'Performance' and 'Security'. A reader counting sections gets two different answers.
fix: Use the same split in both places: either make the text bullet 'Performance' and 'Security' separate, or merge them in the figure.

problem: 'If a section has no effect on a test, cut it' can be read as licence to delete the Introduction, scope and definitions, which the same section says are needed and which traceability depends on. A student may cut the purpose and definitions.
fix: Say: 'Cut any sentence that neither states a requirement nor helps a reader test, trace or interpret one.' Keep purpose, scope and definitions.

problem: Step 2 names the first section 'Scope', but the section order in Section 1 names it 'Introduction' (purpose, scope, definitions, references). Mixing the two names confuses the mapping of step 2 to the recommended order.
fix: Say: 'Use three sections: 1 Introduction (with purpose and scope), 2 Overall Description, 3 Specific Requirements.'

problem: The platform requirement is labelled FR-01, but earlier in the chapter functional requirements are FR and platform/quality limits are NFR. The labelling clashes with the convention the chapter just taught.
fix: Use two non-functional lines, for example NFR-02 (Android 9+) and NFR-03 (Android 10+), and ask which characteristic fails: consistency.
